result.question: How did captain respond to the plan?

readings.answer: He arranged a large night escort to take Paul safely to Felix.
readings.support: Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night. | Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.

readings.answer: He ordered secrecy about the report.
readings.support: Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.
So the commander dismissed the young man

assessments.reason: The commander orders a substantial escort and mounts to take Paul safely to Felix (“Prepare two hundred soldiers… provide mounts for Paul to take him safely”), which is ordering guard protection as in the key.
He also responds by ordering secrecy (“Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me”), a distinct but valid way he handled the reported plan.
“So the commander dismissed the young man” does not address how he acted regarding the plan itself, unlike the protective measures described in the following verses.

result.reason: The passage shows both a secrecy order and arranging a protective escort as responses, so more than one materially different answer fits the question.
